title: Normalized module equivalence and geometric section adjunction
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $k^s/k$ a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure], $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\bar s=\operatorname{Spec}k^s$, and $G=\operatorname{Aut}_k(k^s)$ with its Krull topology. Use small sites in the compatible universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a profinite set $P$ put $T[P]=\varprojlim_i\coprod_{P_i}T$ over its finite quotients [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor].

Let $R$ be any commutative condensed ring, $R_T=p_T^*R$, and use internal modules and ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Write $\mathcal M_R$ for internal condensed $R$-modules and $\mathcal A_G(R)$ for such modules with an $R$-linear action of the condensed group $\underline G(P)=C(P,G)$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module].

Let $a:X\to s$ be a qcqs $k$-scheme. Fix the normalized equivalence $E$ and ring comparison $E(R_s)\cong p_G^{-1}R$ specified in [lem-sfb-field-action-topos-coefficients]. Transport of internal modules gives an exact additive equivalence $E_R:\operatorname{Mod}_{R_s}\simeq\mathcal A_G(R)$ whose section normalization is $(E_RN)(P)=\Gamma(\bar s[P],N|_{\bar s[P]})$ as an $R(P)$-module. Along an action-site arrow $(f,b)$ its restriction is $m\mapsto b\cdot f^*m$; the equivalence identifies internal modules with section-ring module sheaves without changing underlying sections or restrictions. Termwise $E_R$ induces an equivalence of ordinary unbounded derived categories preserving K-injective complexes.

For every map $\varphi:R\to R'$ the comparison $E_R\operatorname{Res}_s\cong\operatorname{Res}_G E_{R'}$ is the identity on section groups, restrictions and action maps, with $R(P)$ acting through $\varphi_P$. Define $F_R=E_Ra_*$ using the actual module pushforward [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. There is a natural identification $(F_RM)(P)=\Gamma(X^s[P],M|_{X^s[P]})$, $X^s=X\times_k k^s$, from the canonical test identification $X\times_s\bar s[P]\cong X^s[P]$, including scalar actions and the action induced by right translations on $G$. Its additive left adjoint is $a^*E_R^{-1}$ with the composite adjunction.

The categories $\operatorname{Mod}_{R_X}$, $\operatorname{Mod}_{R_s}$, $\mathcal M_R$ and $\mathcal A_G(R)$ are Grothendieck abelian. Trivial inflation $\mathcal M_R\to\mathcal A_G(R)$ is exact with additive right adjoint $\Gamma_G$, the submodule of sections fixed after all profinite base changes. Under $E_R$ it is the actual module direct image along $p_s$, equivalently along $p_G$; its adjunction bijection restricts the codomain to invariant sections. These constructions include the zero ring and trivial $G$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-field-action-topos-coefficients] with the given separable closure and the given ring $R$. It supplies the equivalence of set topoi, its section normalization, and the isomorphism of ring objects $E(R_s)\cong p_G^{-1}R$. By [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction] there is an equivalence $\mathscr E^K\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(C_K)$ for the action site $C_K$ of [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation], so the action topos is presented by a small site, and its ring is $R_K=p_K^{-1}R$ with $K=\underline G$. Thus this is an equivalence of ringed topoi to which [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-transport] applies. Reconstruct section-ring module sheaves by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] on both sides. On the action side use the module equivalence in [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation]; by [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], whose actions are natural operations of $C(P,G)$ on the section modules of the same reconstruction, its target is $\mathcal A_G(R)$. The resulting composite is $E_R$. All three comparisons retain underlying section groups; addition and the scalar action are the images of their structure maps. In particular $(E_RN)(P)=N(\bar s[P])$ with its $R(P)$-action, and the action-site restriction along $(f,b)$ is $b\cdot f^*$. This also proves the asserted agreement between the internal and section-ring models.

source.place: Paragraph (3), separable-closure descent input: lift the normalized field equivalence to modules. Agent assembly of the cited ringed-topos statements.

proof.text: The ringed equivalence in the previous step is additive and exact and induces the termwise equivalence on ordinary unbounded derived categories, preserving K-injectives, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-transport]. The internal/section-ring identifications are additive exact equivalences by [lem-sfb-section-ring-lax-pushforward-coherence]. Their action-site counterpart is additive by [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation] and exact by [lem-weil-pbc-equivalence-injective-resolutions]. For completeness these auxiliary equivalences preserve K-injectives directly: a chain map $A\to C(H)I$ from an acyclic complex is, under a quasi-inverse, a chain map $C(H^{-1})A\to I$ from an acyclic complex. A null-homotopy there is carried back termwise, and the unit and counit identify the resulting null-homotopy with one for the original map. The quasi-inverse argument also identifies quasi-isomorphisms, so its termwise unit and counit descend to the mutually inverse unbounded localizations. Hence these changes of module model preserve every claimed property of $E_R$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), ordinary unbounded derived lift of the field equivalence; supporting Stacks Tag 08BJ, derived.tex lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives.

proof.text: Let $\varphi:R\to R'$ and let $N$ be an $R'_s$-module. By [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], scalar restriction retains its underlying object and maps and precomposes its action with $\varphi$. The ring comparison of [lem-sfb-field-action-topos-coefficients] is natural in ring maps. Consequently both $E_R\operatorname{Res}_sN$ and $\operatorname{Res}_GE_{R'}N$ have section group $N(\bar s[P])$ and scalar action $r m=\varphi_P(r)m$. Both have restriction $m\mapsto b\cdot f^*m$ along $(f,b)$, using [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation]. Identity maps on these groups therefore give an equivariant linear natural isomorphism, natural also in $N$ and in $\varphi$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), coefficient-map compatibility of the normalized module equivalence.

proof.text: Use the actual module pushforward of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Its underlying abelian sheaf is the pushforward of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star], so $(E_Ra_*M)(P)=M(X\times_s\bar s[P])$. The base-change isomorphism in [lem-sfb-relative-profinite-test-labels], with $Y=X^s$ over $\bar s$, identifies $X\times_s\bar s[P]=X^s\times_{\bar s}\bar s[P]\cong X^s[P]$, naturally in $P$. This gives the section formula for $F_R$. Its scalar action is restriction of the $R_s$-action through the actual pushforward coefficient map; the equality of internal and sectionwise actions is [lem-sfb-section-ring-lax-pushforward-coherence]. In the free $G$-test presentation, the maps $(g,t)\mapsto(gb(t),f(t))$ of [lem-sfb-field-action-topos-coefficients] become the corresponding maps of these fiber products after base change by $X$. Restriction of $M$ along those maps therefore gives precisely the stated right-translation action and the $b\cdot f^*$ restriction formula, with no choice of a second action.

source.place: Paragraph (3), geometric section functor; Bhatt-Scholze Examples 4.1.9-4.1.10 and the module direct-image definition, Stacks Tag 03D6.

proof.text:
For $A\in\mathcal A_G(R)$ and $M\in\operatorname{Mod}_{R_X}$, the equivalence and the specified module adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] give natural additive bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{R_X}(a^*E_R^{-1}A,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{R_s}(E_R^{-1}A,a_*M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_G(R)}(A,E_Ra_*M).$$
This is exactly the composite adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. The functor $a^*E_R^{-1}$ is additive because each factor is additive. Its unit and counit are the composite ones specified by that node.

source.place: Paragraph (3), left adjoint of the geometric section functor; Stacks Tag 03D7 and categories.tex Tag 0DV0.

proof.text: On the chosen small pro-étale sites of $X$ and $s$, and on the coherent profinite site, reconstructed ring-sheaf modules are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck]. The reconstruction equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] transfers this to $\operatorname{Mod}_{R_X}$, $\operatorname{Mod}_{R_s}$ and $\mathcal M_R$: transport colimits and a generator by the equivalence; preservation of kernels and cokernels by [lem-weil-pbc-equivalence-injective-resolutions] transfers exactness of filtered colimits. A generator remains one since the equivalence is fully faithful. Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-action-grothendieck-inflation] on the profinite site to $K=\underline G$ to obtain the Grothendieck property for $\mathcal E_{\underline G}$ of the reconstructed ring; by [def-sfb-condensed-action-module] and the same reconstruction equivalence, which keeps section modules and is compatible with the sectionwise actions, this is $\mathcal A_G(R)$ with its specified additive structure. Apply its inflation assertion to the map $\underline G\to1$; since $\mathcal E_1(R)=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$, this is additive exact trivial inflation.

source.place: Paragraph (3), existence of the abelian and unbounded derived setting; Stacks injectives.tex Tag 079Q and the small action-site module theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-product-fixed-adjunction] on the coherent profinite site with $K=\underline G$ (and the unused second group trivial). It constructs the additive functor $\Gamma_G$, whose sections are exactly those fixed after every profinite base change, and the adjunction from trivial inflation whose transpose restricts the codomain to these sections. By [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction], the actual module inverse image along $p_G$ is this trivial inflation. The actual direct image, with scalar action induced by its coefficient map, has the module adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Both right adjoints thus represent the same Hom functor: transpose the counit of either adjunction through the other; the triangle identities make these two maps inverse. This identifies $p_{G*}$ with $\Gamma_G$. Under the normalized field equivalence, [lem-sfb-field-action-topos-coefficients] identifies $p_{s*}N(P)$ with the same invariant subobject of $N(\bar s[P])$, by restriction. That inclusion is linear, since its scalar action comes from $R\to p_{s*}R_s$. Hence the set-level comparison is the actual module comparison, and its transpose is the same restriction of codomain. All invoked action statements include the trivial group and zero ring; the displayed formulas also apply to the empty profinite test and the empty scheme, where module sections are zero.
